channel.title: Entuned Blog | Retail Music Strategy
channel.description: Research-backed insights on retail music strategy, in-store customer behavior, and AI-powered audio optimization.

item.title: How to Increase Average Order Value in Retail
item.description: Five levers actually move retail AOV. Why the audio environment is the cheapest one to test, and what 33 years of wine-shop research says about price acceptance.

item.title: How to Increase Dwell Time in Retail Stores
item.description: Five levers that move retail dwell time. Why operators undershoot the easiest one. A two-week test you can run on your own floor against your POS data.

item.title: Music Strategy for the One-Store Brand
item.description: Most retail music writing is built for chains. Here is what actually changes when you run one store, why the smaller footprint cuts both ways, and where to start.

item.title: Your Music Is Already Talking to Your Customers. The Question Is What It's Saying.
item.description: The music playing in your store is already in every sales interaction. It set the customer's emotional register before your associate said a word. Here's what that means for conversion.

item.title: How to Get Out of a Mood Media Contract
item.description: A practical operator walkthrough of exiting a Mood Media contract cleanly. Renewal windows, notice requirements, and what to do before calling legal.

item.title: Mall vs. Street: Making the Same Brand Feel Right in Both
item.description: A mall location and a street location are not the same store. Same brand, different customers, different entry conditions. What multi-location operators get wrong.

item.title: What to Ask Your Music Vendor at the Next QBR
item.description: Ten questions VP Retail Ops should ask their in-store music vendor at the next QBR. Licensing, measurement, staff bypass, cost transparency. Forwardable checklist.

item.title: Tuesday vs. Saturday Traffic: What Your Data Actually Says
item.description: Tuesday traffic and Saturday traffic look like different stores. The gap reveals your real customer mix. Here is how operators should read the pattern.

item.title: Your Store Deserves a Score, Not a Playlist
item.description: A commercial composer designs music to hit specific emotional targets. Retail has always been handed a playlist instead. That gap is what generative audio finally closes.

item.title: AI Music for Business in 2026: What Works
item.description: AI music generation crossed the quality threshold for commercial use. What changed for retail operators paying licensing fees and guessing at playlists.

item.title: Best Background Music for Retail Stores (2026)
item.description: A practical guide for multi-location retailers choosing in-store music in 2026. What to play, what to avoid, and how to stay on the right side of licensing law.

item.title: Is It Actually Illegal to Use Spotify in My Store?
item.description: Is it illegal to play Spotify in your store? Short answer: yes. Here's what the fines look like and what multi-location operators actually use instead.

item.title: Alternatives to Mood Media in 2026: Commercial Music Services Compared
item.description: Mood Media alternatives for multi-location retail in 2026. Soundtrack Your Brand, Cloud Cover, SiriusXM, and AI-original services compared on price, contracts, and measurement.

item.title: The Difference Between Art and Design
item.description: A retail store is a designed space. Every element of it serves the sale or gets in the way. The music belongs in that same category.

item.title: Every Song Is Either Working Or It Isn't
item.description: Your store's music is either helping sales or hurting them. Here's how to tell the difference and what to do about it.

item.title: How Much Does In-Store Music Actually Cost?
item.description: Retail music runs $17 to $80 per location per month for the subscription. The real bill includes licensing, hardware, and invoices nobody tracks as one line.

item.title: How to Make Your Store Sound Premium
item.description: What makes a store sound expensive? Not the genre. The right music lifts willingness to pay 8-12%. Here's what operators at every price point can learn from it.

item.title: How to Measure If Your Store Music Is Working
item.description: If you cannot answer whether your store music helps or hurts sales, you are not alone. A short audit for operators who want a defensible answer.

item.title: Audio Advertising vs. Audio Strategy
item.description: QSIC and retail media networks sell ads through your speakers. Audio strategy uses music to sell your products. These are fundamentally different approaches.

item.title: Song Selection Is Not Music Strategy
item.description: Retailers have known for decades that music changes buying behavior. Most are still picking songs the wrong way. Here is what song selection misses.
